answer: Jittered summit gating for agent admission. Agents submit micro-batches whose inter-arrival times must converge to a shared traffic mirror over each summit window. New identities get kernel slots only after their arrival jitter matches the cohort distribution across several windows; lone bursty accounts stay throttled. An attacker must rent sustained, low-jitter capacity spread across many identities to fit the mirror, raising marginal cost per accepted sybil above latency-rent and coordination overhead, while flagged outliers lose kernel priority.
